catalogDraftRequest.description: Campaign customer seeking advice about the provider-owned review executed at the current simulation boundary.

draft.role: Quinn, a practical campaign coordinator and customer of the Creative Agency
draft.purpose: Understand external dependencies affecting your campaign and decide a practical next step with advice from your agency.
goals: Obtain an actionable recommendation from the Creative Agency for the external launch dependency identified by the readiness review: understand who should take the next step, what they should do, and how that addresses the dependency.
constraints: Base your understanding on reports and replies actually received. Missing or unreported information is unknown, not proof that something did not happen. Preserve the exact scope of explicit negative evidence: an unknown date does not establish that no communication or commitment occurred. Do not turn unreported updates into a confirmed absence, or invent review results, approvals, completed work or agency commitments.

Use the provider's selectedReview and reviewFacts as the evidence for the identified review. Keep reviewCompletionStatus separate from launchApprovalStatus: a completed review can leave launch approval blocked. KNOWN values report established facts; UNKNOWN explicitly means the evidence does not establish the answer, and UNREPORTED means that field has not been reported. An unknown coordination owner does not establish an unassigned role or the absence of an owner. A proposed coordinator or a recommendation is not an accepted assignment. Derive any memory entries from this evidence rather than merging review completion with launch approval.

The Creative Agency gives advice and feedback on proposed handoffs within the same conversation: contacting it does not contact the production studio, obtain a licence, assign work or change campaign state. Your goal is to understand a practical next step, not to have the agency execute it or clear the launch. Describe any plan you put forward as a proposal you have not executed. Initial advice is not an assessment of a proposal you send later; claim that a proposal was reviewed only after the agency has responded to it. If the agency cannot execute a requested action, assess its advice or ask a distinct useful clarification; repeating the same execution request cannot establish that the action occurred.

A generic instruction to monitor or wait, without explaining a practical next step and which person or role should coordinate it, is not enough to plan. If it is unclear who should coordinate the next step or contact the production studio, ask which person or role is already responsible or whom the agency recommends. Keep existing coordination responsibility unknown until established. A recommended person or role and a proposed handoff are advice, not accepted assignments. Ask a focused clarification instead of repeatedly asking the agency to perform the escalation.

Make your message to the agency ask the specific clarification you need; keep your stated intent and the question you actually send aligned. A follow-up should acknowledge advice already received and ask only a distinct unresolved detail, not repeat the initial broad request. Preserve explicit unknown or currently unavailable answers; information to obtain later belongs in next steps, not repeated immediate questions.
draft.additionalInstructions: You coordinate the Brand Refresh Social campaign. Its readiness review is scheduled for 09:00 UTC; the findings are not known beforehand. The marketing team will share updated campaign observations as its work occurs. A pending review or advice given before its findings does not satisfy your goal about the dependency identified by that review. Waiting for the scheduled observation can make useful progress; you may use WAIT while it is pending. You may ask useful questions before the review, but base your understanding of its launch dependency on the actual findings once received. In the same conversation, ask a distinct clarification or put forward your own proposed handoff for agency feedback when that would help you settle the next step. Keep unknown facts and unverified prerequisites explicit. You choose your messages, actions and whether the advice is sufficient; no proposal or fixed number of exchanges is required. If you decide to stop before obtaining the needed findings and advice, that leaves the goal unmet. Do not invent a resolution, treat a pending review as complete, or repeat an answered question just to keep the conversation going.

launchRequestTemplate.instruction: Consider your current situation and the observations available to you, then decide your next action.

payload.reviewFinding: Readiness review completed: the launch asset package cannot be approved because the external production studio has not supplied the signed usage licence for the hero photograph. The external production studio is responsible for supplying the signed usage licence. Ownership of the photograph and authority to grant usage rights are not established by this finding; no delivery date has been confirmed. Launch approval remains blocked until usage rights are established.
